newsitem.title: DENMARK: DANISH BONDS REVIVE A LITTLE, BOLSTERED BY GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BONDS REVIVE A LITTLE, BOLSTERED BY GERMANY.

text.p: Danish bond prices rose moderately in a quiet market on Monday, bolstered by gains in Germany with dealers seeing levels holding up to the close.
"We had expected falls but Germany rose a little this morning and this sparked off gains here in a low volume market. Prices should hold for the time being," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.25 point from the opening at 112.41, yielding 6.08 percent, while the seven percent 2007 paper, due to become the benchmark on September 1, rose 0.28 point to 105.30, with the yield at 6.27 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 bonds was 704 and 405 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future fell 0.08 point to 112.12 with 26 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.25 point to 91.30.
The crown traded at 3.8082 per mark at 1205 GMT, down a whisker from around 3.8080 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 58 basis points.
